candidates.description: filterTargetsByCreatureSubtype implements the target_filter_creature_subtype
candidates.doc:
filterTargetsByCreatureSubtype implements the target_filter_creature_subtype
primitive (ticket engine.auto-target-filter-creature-subtype-eff5ac9036,
Snarling Undorak class): "Target Beast creature gets +1/+1 until end of
turn." Narrows an already-chosen targets slice, at the same
before-the-switch chokepoint as resolveSameNameAsTargetFilter just above,
to only the targets that are creatures carrying the given subtype
(Card.SubTypes, Rule 201.4 exact-name match, mirroring
resolvePumpGlobalFilterTargets's exclude_subtype check one primitive
below). A target that fails the check is simply dropped rather than
causing an error, matching Rule 601.2c/608.2b's "illegal target" handling
used elsewhere in this file (e.g.
executeDestroyTargetIfManaValueEqualsUnspentMana above).
candidates.name: filterTargetsByCreatureSubtype
candidates.title: filterTargetsByCreatureSubtype

candidates.description: executeDestroyMultiFilterTargets destroys N simultaneous REQUIRED targets
candidates.doc:
executeDestroyMultiFilterTargets destroys N simultaneous REQUIRED targets
in one resolution, each validated against its OWN positional filter
(Decimate class: "Destroy target artifact, target creature, target
enchantment, and target land."), unlike destroyAllMatching just above
(whole battlefield, one shared filter) and
executeDestroyUpToArtifactCreatureLand (optional slots, no filter
mismatch possible since each slot is type-fixed by the caller).
effectValue["filters"][i] gates targets[i]; a target that doesn't match
its own slot's filter is simply excluded from the simultaneous
destruction (cast-time legality is expected to have already required a
legal choice per slot). Victims are snapshotted by pointer before any of
them is destroyed, same simultaneous-destruction idiom as
destroyAllMatching, so destroying an earlier target can't affect whether
a later target still matches its own filter.
candidates.name: executeDestroyMultiFilterTargets
candidates.title: executeDestroyMultiFilterTargets

candidates.description: executeDestroyTargetWithFilter implements the destroy_target_with_filter
candidates.doc:
executeDestroyTargetWithFilter implements the destroy_target_with_filter
primitive (ticket engine.auto-creature-with-power-n-or-greater-ac0c378c29,
Skywhaler's Shot class): "Destroy target creature with power 3 or
greater." Unlike executeDestroyTargetWithMaxManaValue's bespoke CMC
ceiling just above, this reuses matchesPermanentFilter (gamestate.go) —
the SAME filter vocabulary "destroy all X" mass effects already use,
including its massFilterCmpRe power/toughness/mv threshold suffix
("creature_power_gte_3") — so a single-target destroy can be gated by a
numeric power predicate without inventing a new one-off comparison. A
target missing from the battlefield, or failing the filter, is skipped
rather than failing the whole effect (Rule 601.2c partial-legality),
matching the sibling destroy-with-a-condition executors below. Plain
"destroy target creature"/"destroy target artifact"/etc. never call this
executor, so they remain unaffected (negative example: no power
predicate is added where none was requested).
candidates.name: executeDestroyTargetWithFilter
candidates.title: executeDestroyTargetWithFilter

candidates.description: executeDestroyMultiFilterTargets destroys N simultaneous REQUIRED targets
candidates.doc:
executeDestroyMultiFilterTargets destroys N simultaneous REQUIRED targets
in one resolution, each validated against its OWN positional filter
(Decimate class: "Destroy target artifact, target creature, target
enchantment, and target land."), unlike destroyAllMatching just above
(whole battlefield, one shared filter) and
executeDestroyUpToArtifactCreatureLand (optional slots, no filter
mismatch possible since each slot is type-fixed by the caller).
effectValue["filters"][i] gates targets[i]; a target that doesn't match
its own slot's filter is simply excluded from the simultaneous
destruction (cast-time legality is expected to have already required a
legal choice per slot). Victims are snapshotted by pointer before any of
them is destroyed, same simultaneous-destruction idiom as
destroyAllMatching, so destroying an earlier target can't affect whether
a later target still matches its own filter.

greater." Unlike executeDestroyTargetWithMaxManaValue's bespoke CMC
ceiling just above, this reuses matchesPermanentFilter (gamestate.go) —
the SAME filter vocabulary "destroy all X" mass effects already use,
including its massFilterCmpRe power/toughness/mv threshold suffix
("creature_power_gte_3") — so a single-target destroy can be gated by a

candidates.description: executeGrantValuedKeywordFilteredUntilEOT implements the
candidates.doc:
executeGrantValuedKeywordFilteredUntilEOT implements the
grant_valued_keyword_until_eot primitive (ticket
engine.auto-grant-valued-keyword-until-eot-1312f3366b, Plague Nurse
class): "Each other creature you control with toxic gains toxic 1 until
end of turn." Extends grant_keywords_until_eot's group-grant branch (the
"creature"/"permanent" AffectsFilter case in ExecuteAbilityEffect below)
for a VALUED keyword: unlike a plain presence keyword (flying, haste,
...), which HasKeywordWithEffects reads live off the EffectManager and
never needs a concrete number, Toxic's amount lives on the plain
Card.ToxicN field that combat.go's poison-counter check reads
UNCONDITIONALLY (not through the EffectManager) — so a lazily-evaluated
filter effect alone can't feed it a number. Recipients are resolved NOW:
every OTHER creature (source itself is always excluded, matching the
"each other" shape this primitive targets) the controller controls that
ALREADY has requiredKeyword (Rule 702.164b: multiple toxic instances on
one permanent COMPOUND rather than overriding, matching the "with
toxic" gate on the source Oracle text) — a creature lacking it is
skipped entirely, not granted toxic from nothing. value is added
directly onto each match's ToxicN, and one AffectsSpecific/UntilEOT
ContinuousEffect per recipient records the same delta in
GrantKeywordValue purely so CleanupEndOfTurnEffects can subtract it
back off when the grant expires.

for a VALUED keyword: unlike a plain presence keyword (flying, haste,
...), which HasKeywordWithEffects reads live off the EffectManager and
never needs a concrete number, Toxic's amount lives on the plain
Card.ToxicN field that combat.go's poison-counter check reads
UNCONDITIONALLY (not through the EffectManager) — so a lazily-evaluated
filter effect alone can't feed it a number. Recipients are resolved NOW:
every OTHER creature (source itself is always excluded, matching the
"each other" shape this primitive targets) the controller controls that
ALREADY has requiredKeyword (Rule 702.164b: multiple toxic instances on
one permanent COMPOUND rather than overriding, matching the "with
toxic" gate on the source Oracle text) — a creature lacking it is
skipped entirely, not granted toxic from nothing. value is added
directly onto each match's ToxicN, and one AffectsSpecific/UntilEOT
ContinuousEffect per recipient records the same delta in
GrantKeywordValue purely so CleanupEndOfTurnEffects can subtract it
back off when the grant expires.
